title: Add a check() deny-path test — the gate has only a happy-path test today
description:
## Why

**The gate has one test and it only proves the happy path.** `test/auth-broker-gate.test.ts:295` is *"uses agent.capabilities as scopes when the API key carries no scopes override"* — a pass-through assertion. There is no test asserting that an under-scoped principal is **denied**.

This is the authorization path. Epics 4 and 5 both hang new gates off it (`requiresSigner`, `requiresAccess`, the resolver membrane). Adding those on top of a deny-path with no coverage is how a membrane silently becomes a sieve.

Note `broker-impl.ts:274-280` already documents a fail-closed intent: *"FGA on `need.resource` is async; callers asking for it must use `gate()`, not `check()`. We treat its presence here as a programming error — fail closed."* That fail-closed branch is untested.

## What to test

- [ ] `check()` **denies** when the granted scope does not satisfy the requirement (`scopeSatisfies` false).
- [ ] `check()` **fails closed** when `need.resource` is present — the documented programming-error branch at `broker-impl.ts:274-280`.
- [ ] Deny when the agent record has no scope and no capabilities at all.
- [ ] Deny on a scope that is broader than granted (`narrows` violation) — i.e. no privilege escalation via a child scope.
- [ ] L0 anonymous identity is denied anything above L0 (`AuthBroker.identify()` returns L0 and never throws, `broker-impl.ts:276` — absence of a credential must not read as absence of a restriction).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each bullet above is a named test in `test/auth-broker-gate.test.ts`.
- [ ] Tests fail if the deny branch is removed (verify by temporarily inverting the check).
- [ ] `npm test` green.

## Size: S

title: Add Agent.scope?: Scope alongside capabilities; read-both in resolveAgentIdentity
description:
## Why

The agent record and the broker are the two places the string vocabulary is load-bearing.

**Current state, verbatim:**
- `src/sdk/types.ts:122` — `capabilities: string[]` on the `Agent` interface.
- `src/sdk/auth/broker-impl.ts:523` — `scopes: overlay.scopes ?? agent.capabilities`, under the comment *"Agent capabilities are the new scope vocabulary; broker prefers overlay scopes (from the API key) when set, else falls back to the agent's full capability set."* The line immediately below (`:525`) already carries `scope: overlay.scope` with the comment *"Structured Scope is a property of the key, not the agent row."*

So the structured `Scope` exists on the **key** overlay but not on the **agent**. That asymmetry is the bug this issue closes.

## What to do

1. Add `Agent.scope?: Scope` (from `src/sdk/auth/scope.ts`) **alongside** `capabilities: string[]` in `src/sdk/types.ts`. Optional, additive — no migration cliff.
2. Make `resolveAgentIdentity` (`src/sdk/auth/broker-impl.ts`, around `:523`) **read both**: prefer the structured `Scope` when present, fall back to the string array. Same precedence shape the overlay already uses.
3. Map at the AAP wire boundary (`worker/routes/aap.ts`) so the published `capabilities` field is unchanged in both directions.

## Non-goals

- Do **not** rename the AAP wire field `capabilities`. It stays verbatim.
- Do **not** delete `Agent.capabilities` in this issue. Read-both is the point; removal is a later, separate decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Agent.scope?: Scope` declared in `src/sdk/types.ts`.
- [ ] `resolveAgentIdentity` reads structured `Scope` first, string `capabilities` second; both paths tested.
- [ ] AAP responses byte-compatible with before (regression test on `worker/routes/aap.ts`).
- [ ] `scopeSatisfies` / `narrows` used for the structured comparison rather than a re-implemented string match.
- [ ] `npm test` green.

title: Publish /.well-known/agents.json — MCP interface + identity ladder + probes
description:
## Why

**This is the single highest-ROI issue in the id.org.ai backlog.** The MCP server is live at `https://id.org.ai/mcp` and passes its own tests; no discovery surface announces it, so api.qa cannot see it and 6 MCP-OAuth checks are *skipped* rather than passed.

Publishing one static JSON document flips AX checks **2** (agents.json capability card parses), **6** (MCP interface declared — transport + tools), **7** (keyless flow: a declared endpoint answers 2xx with no key), and **10** (attestation/identity ladder declared), and un-skips the MCP-OAuth check group.

## What to publish

`/.well-known/agents.json` declaring:

- **MCP interface** — transport, `url: https://id.org.ai/mcp`, and the **3 tools that are actually live at L0** and only those: `explore`, `search`, `fetch` (`worker/routes/mcp.ts:116-155`; the tool/level map is at `worker/routes/mcp.ts:332` — `{ explore: 0, search: 0, fetch: 0, try: 1, do: 1 }`). `try` and `do` are L1+ and must be declared with their level, or omitted — declaring them as freely callable is a `claims-honesty` failure.
- **Attestation / identity ladder** — the L0-L3 `CapabilityLevel` progression (`src/sdk/mcp/auth.ts`), including that L0 is anonymous and keyless.
- **Probes** — the keyless entry points an agent can call with no credential to get first value (check 7). `AuthBroker.identify()` returns the L0 anonymous identity and never throws (`src/sdk/auth/broker-impl.ts:276`), so a keyless probe is genuinely safe to declare.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET https://id.org.ai/.well-known/agents.json` returns 200 with `Content-Type: application/json` and parses.
- [ ] The declared MCP `url` resolves and speaks MCP; declared tool names match `worker/routes/mcp.ts` exactly.
- [ ] The declared keyless probe returns 2xx with no `Authorization` header.
- [ ] The identity/attestation ladder is declared.
- [ ] api.qa checks 2, 6, 7, 10 flip to pass; MCP-OAuth checks move from skipped to passing.
- [ ] No `claims-honesty` failure: nothing declared that is not live.

title: ADR 0012 M5: authz-path realignment (capabilities -> Scope)
description:
## Why

ADR 0012 M5 splits the authority nouns: a **`Capability`** is a *can-do* (ability), a **`Scope`** is a *may-do* (authorization). id.org.ai currently uses the string array `Agent.capabilities` on the authorization path — the wrong noun on the load-bearing path.

**Half the work is already done.** `src/sdk/auth/scope.ts` ships a real structured `Scope`, tested:
- `ScopeGrant { verb, resource, ceiling }` (`scope.ts:54`), `Scope` (`scope.ts:71`), `ScopeRequirement` (`scope.ts:79`), `Measure` (`scope.ts:31`)
- `resourceMatches` (`:111`), `scopeSatisfies` (`:192`), `narrows` (`:206`), `deriveChildScope` (`:226`), `isScope` (`:234`)

What is missing is that the *agent record* and the *broker* still speak strings.

## Why it is first

This epic is **small** and is a **prerequisite for Epics 4 and 5**:
- ADR 0016 blast radius, id.org.ai row: *"The `Agent.capabilities` -> `Scope` realignment already queued (ADR 0012 M5) **is the same authz path**"* as the credential gates.
- id.org.ai ADR 0001 D6 aligns the resolver's authorization vocabulary to ADR 0012 — the resolved principal's authorization is a `Scope` at a tier, not a `Capability`.

Building `requiresSigner` / `requiresAccess` (Epic 4) or the resolver membrane (Epic 5) on top of a string array means doing it twice.

## Hard constraint for the whole epic

**The AAP wire term `capabilities` stays verbatim.** The Agent Auth Protocol v1.0 surface (`worker/routes/aap.ts`, shipped in closed bead `id-9s0`) is a published external contract. This epic is an **internal** realignment with a mapping at the wire boundary. Renaming the wire field is out of scope and would be a breaking protocol change.

title: AXP Tier 0: discovery surfaces (F -> A-/B+)
description:
## Why

api.qa grades `id.org.ai` an **F** today, and the reason is not missing capability — it is missing *announcement*. The MCP interface at `https://id.org.ai/mcp` is live and tested (`worker/routes/mcp.ts`, tools `explore`/`search`/`fetch` at L0+, `try`/`do` at L1+), the OAuth 2.1 provider is shipped, the identity ladder L0-L3 works. Nothing on the domain tells an agent any of that.

This epic is the highest-ROI block in the whole backlog: it is **pure publication of already-passing behavior**. No new runtime capability is built. Per api.qa's `DESIGN.md` §"The AX score (R-k's 10 points, made executable)", this epic targets checks **1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10** and un-skips the 6 MCP-OAuth checks the code already passes.

Target: **F -> A-/B+** (grade bands, api.qa `DESIGN.md`: 9 -> A, 7-8 -> B, 5-6 -> C).

## Definition of done

`id.org.ai/specs/axp-acceptance.spec.json` — an api.qa **PinnedSpec** being authored in parallel — is the acceptance contract for this epic. Do not block on it existing; build to the AX rubric and wire the spec in when it lands.

```
npx api.qa verify https://id.org.ai --spec specs/axp-acceptance.spec.json --expect-digest <pin>
```

Local mode is advisory (`attested: false`); the deployed api.qa verdict is the real gate (api.qa `DESIGN.md` attack #6).

## Warning inherited by every child

api.qa's two non-scoring honesty checks — `schema-conformance` and `claims-honesty` — **cap the grade at C** regardless of score if a published surface lies (api.qa `DESIGN.md` attack #11). Every surface published here must describe what the worker actually does. Do not declare a tool, an endpoint, or an auth mode that is not live.

title: The Who wiring — GET stages, POST captures — through AuthBroker.identify()
description:
## Why

**This is the thesis.** ADR 0013 R3: a Digital Link resolution answers What/Where/When/Why/How; the **Who** — the scanning principal — is what a bare product resolver leaves empty. id.org.ai supplies it *because it is the identity layer*: the same attested session that dereferences the key names the principal, so **resolution and capture happen under one identity**, and the Who is a first-class principal **including an `agent_…`** — a scanning principal EPCIS never modeled.

## The mechanism (R15, restated in ADR 0001 D3)

- **A scan is a GET: it resolves the key and *stages* a candidate event.**
- **The EPCIS event is minted only on capture (POST)** — attested, membrane-governed, landing as a CBV-typed event in the object's **owning startup's G5 books**.
- **Not every scan writes.** An unattested scan resolves the public lens (`gs1:pip`) with `Who` absent and no G5 confirmation (R13's existence-neutral gate). *"'Adds the Who' is precisely the delta authentication buys."*

## The build is smaller than it looks

id.org.ai ADR 0001, verbatim: *"**we already have the Who.** `AuthBroker.identify(req)` (`broker-impl.ts:276`) resolves the principal from any request's credential, returning the **L0 anonymous identity when none is presented and never throwing**. The resolver does not need a new identity mechanism — it needs to route GS1 keys through the broker and attach the resolved principal to the staged/captured event."*

The never-throws property is what makes the anonymous path work without a second code path: R13's existence-neutral gate falls out of `identify()` returning L0 rather than erroring.

## Honest scope of the claim (do not overbuild the marketing)

ADR 0013 R3's adversarial-review correction: it is *not* that a plain resolver structurally cannot carry a Who. The narrower, still load-bearing claim is that id.org.ai supplies it **natively, by default, under one attested session spanning resolve->capture, with agents as first-class principals**. Build to that.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] GET route runs the request through `AuthBroker.identify()` and stages a candidate event with the resolved principal as `Who`.
- [ ] POST capture mints the EPCIS event, membrane-governed, with `Who` attached.
- [ ] Anonymous GET resolves `gs1:pip` with **`Who` absent**, no staging write, no G5 confirmation (R13) — and does not throw.
- [ ] `agent_…` principals are first-class `Who` values, tested (ADR 0013 walk 3 — the verification agent dereferencing an SGTIN).
- [ ] Walk 1 test: attested pharmacist scan -> GET resolves the SGTIN, POST capture mints a CBV `dispensing` event with `Who = human_<pharmacist>`.
- [ ] Walk 2 test: signed-in shopper scanning a bare GTIN produces a CBV-**extension** `inspecting` event (R6 — a consumer authenticity check is not a supply-chain step), not `receiving`.
- [ ] Authorization on the membrane path is a `Scope` at a tier, not a `Capability` (ADR 0001 D6) — requires Epic 3.

## Size: L

title: The 303-vs-200 content-negotiation matrix
description:
## Why

A GS1-conformant resolver's redirect behavior is not a free choice — it is where conformance is actually tested, and it is the axis where "conform completely at the seam" (ADR 0013 R1) either holds or does not. A stock GS1 scanner, a POS at Sunrise 2027, a browser, and an agent asking for JSON-LD all hit the same address and must each get the right thing.

## The matrix to define and test

Enumerate every cell of (request shape) x (response), and pick 303 vs 200 deliberately for each:

- **default resolution** (browser-ish `Accept: text/html`, no `linkType`) -> **303** to the `gs1:defaultLink` target (`gs1:pip`)
- **`?linkType=linkset`** / **`Accept: application/linkset+json`** -> **200** with the RFC 9264 linkset, **no redirect** (R2 states this explicitly)
- **`?linkType=<specific>`** -> 303 to that target
- **`Accept: application/ld+json`** -> the object's JSON-LD carrying the canonical `{type}_{sqid}` `$id` with the GS1 URI as `sameAs` (R2/R5/R14)
- **`Accept: text/markdown`** -> agent-legible markdown (consistent with Epic 1's root content negotiation)
- **unauthenticated + instance/lot grain** -> the membrane behavior, not a leak (R7: class = public/cacheable; instance/lot = membrane-gated per regime)
- **unknown `linkType`** -> defined, conformant fallback
- `Vary` correctness so caches never cross-serve representations

## Why it is its own issue

The 303-vs-200 split interacts with grain (R7) and with the membrane (R4/R13): the *same* address answers differently for an anonymous scan and an attested one, and differently again for a class key vs a controlled lot. Getting that matrix right by accident is unlikely; it needs to be written down and tested cell by cell.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Matrix documented in the repo (a table, in `docs/`), then implemented.
- [ ] Every cell has a test.
- [ ] Linkset path never redirects.
- [ ] `Vary` set correctly on every negotiated response.
- [ ] Anonymous instance/lot request does not leak membrane-gated data.
- [ ] Behavior checked against the GS1-Conformant Resolver Standard.

## Size: M

title: RFC 9264 linkset + gs1:defaultLink configuration
description:
## Why

ADR 0013 R2, verbatim: *"Content negotiation and `?linkType=` behave exactly as RESOLVER.md §3 rules, with GS1's **`gs1:defaultLink`** as the configurable default target (commonly `gs1:pip` for consumer products) and `?linkType=linkset` / `Accept: application/linkset+json` returning the **RFC 9264** linkset."*

This is a named GS1 conformance requirement, not a nicety: the GS1-Conformant Resolver Standard specifies linkset behavior, and an unauthenticated scan must still resolve the public product page (`gs1:pip`) with `Who` absent (R4 / R13's existence-neutral gate).

## What to build

- **`gs1:defaultLink` configuration** — per-object (or per-brand) default link type, commonly `gs1:pip` for consumer products. Configurable, not hardcoded.
- **RFC 9264 linkset** returned for `?linkType=linkset` and for `Accept: application/linkset+json`. **No redirect** on the linkset path.
- `?linkType=<type>` selecting a specific target.

## Reuse

Epic 2's linkset / `Link`-header issue builds an RFC 9264 representation for the AXP discovery surfaces. **Reuse that machinery**; this issue adds GS1 link types to it rather than forking a second linkset implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gs1:defaultLink` configurable; `gs1:pip` the common default for consumer products.
- [ ] `?linkType=linkset` returns an RFC 9264 linkset, **no redirect**.
- [ ] `Accept: application/linkset+json` returns the same, content-negotiated.
- [ ] `?linkType=<specific>` resolves to that target.
- [ ] Unauthenticated request resolves the public `gs1:pip` lens with `Who` absent, no G5 write (R4/R13).
- [ ] Shares the Epic 2 linkset implementation.
- [ ] Validated against the GS1-Conformant Resolver Standard's linkset expectations.

## Size: M

title: GS1 URI-syntax parser + grain routing by key semantics (not AI 21 alone)
description:
## Why

The parser is the front door: `https://id.org.ai/01/{gtin}[/21/{serial}]` and further GS1 Application Identifiers as path/query (ADR 0013 R2). It must be GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax conformant — a stock GS1 scanner has to work against it with zero knowledge of us (R1).

## The routing rule — and the specific mistake to avoid

ADR 0013 **R7** is titled, verbatim: *"The grain split: instance keys vs class keys, routed by GS1 key semantics **(not by AI `21` alone)**"*.

Route by **key semantics**, not by the presence of a serial AI:

| Key | AIs | Grain |
|---|---|---|
| **SGTIN** | `01` + `21` | instance (serialized) |
| **SSCC** | `00` | instance — serial is intrinsic; there is no `21` |
| **GIAI** | `8004` | instance — individual asset |
| **GRAI** | `8003` | instance — returnable asset |
| **LGTIN** | `01` + `10` | **lot/batch** — EPCIS `epcClass`; neither pure class nor serialized instance |
| **GTIN** | `01` alone | class |

Routing on AI `21` alone gets **SSCC, GIAI, and GRAI wrong** (all instance-grain, none carry `21`) and gets **LGTIN wrong** (carries `10`, not `21`).

## Why grain matters beyond parsing

R7 ties grain to the tier/membrane split: **class = public/cacheable**; **instance/lot = membrane-gated per the product's regime**. R7 verbatim on the lot case: *"a lot-managed unit (much pharma is lot-tracked, not serialized) is **not** public by default; the veto against publishing a controlled lot on the class tier."* A parser that mislabels an LGTIN as a class key leaks a controlled lot.

Also (R2/R5): the parsed URI is an **address**. It dereferences via the registry to the object's canonical `{type}_{sqid}` `$id` and is never itself an `$id` — no string-constructed targets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] GS1 Digital Link URI syntax parser, conformant to the published syntax standard.
- [ ] Grain routing implemented by key semantics; all six rows above covered by tests.
- [ ] Explicit negative test: a routing rule keyed on AI `21` alone fails the SSCC / GIAI / GRAI / LGTIN cases.
- [ ] LGTIN routes to lot grain and inherits the product's regime — not public by default.
- [ ] Parsed address dereferences via the registry to a canonical `$id`; the GS1 URI appears as `sameAs`, never as the `$id`.
- [ ] Unknown/unsupported AIs handled without 500s.
- [ ] Test vector: `https://id.org.ai/01/00840034001234/21/A1B2C3` (ADR 0013's own worked example, a serialized pharma unit).

title: Implement the requiresAccess demand gate
description:
## Why

The demand-side half of ADR 0016 C3, verbatim: *"**Demand side (new, symmetric):** a restricted Upstream declares **`requiresAccess: <credential-type>`**; id.org.ai denies consumption unless the calling principal holds a live credential conferring that `access` scope."*

C2's whole point is that this is the *same primitive from the other market side*: a Manheim dealer license lets you **consign** (supply, `perform:`) *and* **buy wholesale** (demand, `access:`); a state bar lets you **perform** reserved acts *and* **access** CM/ECF and sealed dockets. ADR 0016 Consequences: *"The demand side is unified. The possibility-surface's scattered access gates (identity-gated, statute-restricted, account-required, sanctioned S2S) collapse into `requiresAccess` — symmetric to the reserved-leaf `requiresSigner`."*

## Named instances

OpenEvidence's physician gate, PACER/CM-ECF, FinCEN BOI, Manheim inventory access, Westlaw.

## The enforcement is deliberately lighter — and that is a ruling, not a shortcut

`requiresAccess` gates **read/consume**; `requiresSigner` gates **the act** (composing with the drivly read/record/act triad, R-z). ADR 0016 walk 3 (OpenEvidence, **CLICKS-WITH-TIEBREAK**) marks the boundary: OpenEvidence's real gate is *NPI-existence against NPPES — enumeration, not board-status*. That is acceptable for a light demand gate and **explicitly not acceptable for a reserved act** (the `identifier != good standing` law).

So the access gate may be satisfiable by an identifier check with a cached TTL — but the policy table must record *which* level of check a given `requiresAccess` demands, and it must be impossible for a reserved act to be routed through this lighter path.

## Level-dependence

C4: access tends **entity-held** (the dealership's Manheim membership, the firm's PACER/Westlaw account). So the two-part check matters more here than on the perform face: *holder (the org) in good standing* **AND** *the calling principal is an authorized rep of the holder* (derived deputized Representation).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `requiresAccess: <credential-type>` declarable on a restricted resource.
- [ ] Denies consumption when the calling principal holds no credential conferring the matching `access` scope.
- [ ] Entity-held case works: org holds the credential, an authorized rep calls, the two-part check passes; a non-rep of the same org is denied.
- [ ] Uses the effect-class policy table (read/consume -> cached TTL permitted).
- [ ] Structurally impossible for a `requiresSigner` reserved act to be satisfied by an `requiresAccess`-grade check — tested.
- [ ] Symmetry test: one credential (the dealer license) satisfies both a `perform: consign:wholesale` gate and an `access: manheim:wholesale` gate — ADR 0016 walk 2, the keystone binder.

Blocked by the DECISION issue; depends on `verify()`. Requires Epic 3.

## Size: M

title: Wire the ordered M8 -> requiresSigner supply gate into AuthBroker.gate()
description:
## Why

This is where the credential model becomes enforcement. ADR 0016 **C3**, verbatim:

> **On top of M8**, a **reserved act** may additionally declare **`requiresSigner: <credential-type>`**: where present, the human signer M8 already forced must *also* hold a live `Credential` conferring the matching `perform` scope. **id.org.ai's membrane denies otherwise.** … Two ordered gates: *is the signer a human?* (M8) -> *does that human hold the required credential?* (C3).

## The ordering is load-bearing and must be structural

**M8 first, credential second.** ADR 0016 C3 is explicit that the credential requirement **layers onto** M8 and does not replace it: *"ADR 0012 M8's two-signer taint … **That taint is unchanged.** A kestrel `broker|live` countersignature still requires a **human with legal capacity — not a licensed professional**; it is a pure M8 human-capacity taint and carries **no** `Credential`."*

So:
- `broker|live` is **not** a credential instance. If the implementation treats every M8-tainted act as credential-gated, C3 has been misread.
- The genuinely credential-gated leaves are the **patent-bar filing, the notary jurat, the CPA attestation** (walks 1 and 4).
- Evaluating the credential check before or instead of the human-capacity check would let a non-human principal holding a credential reference pass. The order must be enforced by the code path, not by convention.

## Also keep distinct

`requiresSigner` is a **requirement declaration on the act-type**. It is **not** patent.click's `Attestation { authority: 'PatentAttorney' }`, which is an **M6-category citing field on the resulting event** — a receipt citing the authority the act was performed under, parallel to (not the same slot as) M6's frozen `authority: mandate_…`. M6's sense-split holds: the `@org.ai/authority` kernel is the *gate*; an `authority:` field is a *citation, never a gate* (ADR 0016 F1/F2).

## Where it goes

`AuthBroker.gate()` — the async path. `broker-impl.ts:274-280` already documents why: *"FGA on `need.resource` is async; callers asking for it must use `gate()`, not `check()`."* A credential verification is a network read; it belongs in `gate()` for the same reason.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `requiresSigner: <credential-type>` declarable on an act-type.
- [ ] `AuthBroker.gate()` evaluates **M8 human-capacity first**, credential second — ordering enforced structurally and tested with a case that would pass if reordered.
- [ ] `broker|live` passes M8 and requires **no** credential (regression test — this is the specific misreading C3 warns against).
- [ ] A reserved act with `requiresSigner` denies when the human signer lacks the matching `perform` scope.
- [ ] The check consumes the freshness policy table: reserved act -> fresh check (walk 5 test passes at this layer too).
- [ ] The gate result is a `{credentialRef, jurisdiction}` reference, and the emitted event carries the authority **citation** — the two are visibly different fields in the code.
- [ ] Deny is the default on any error path.

Blocked by the DECISION issue; depends on `verify()` and the freshness policy table. Requires Epic 3 (this is a `Scope` check with `source: Credential`).

## Size: L

title: Effect-class -> freshness-TTL policy table (reserved acts require a fresh check)
description:
## Why

ADR 0016 C5, verbatim: *"**Liveness by effect-class:** a **reserved act** or **act-class** transaction requires a **fresh** good-standing check (a suspended attorney is blocked at `file.patent` exactly as a lapsed dealer is stopped at the lane); **read/record** may use a cached attestation with a TTL."*

The effect-class triad is **read / record / act** (drivly `RULINGS-2026-07-19-SESSION-3` R-z — note ADR 0016 L-a corrects an earlier miscitation: this is a drivly ruling, **not** an ADR 0012 ruling).

ADR 0016 leaves the actual numbers open — Consequences, *"Open, not ruled here: … (b) the freshness-TTL values per effect-class (C5 — a policy knob)"*. This issue closes that knob.

## The mapping already exists

This is **not** a new caching layer. It is a policy table over the src.do data contract: `cacheTtl` / `staleTtl` + the `freshness` field. A reserved act demands a fresh read; read/record can accept a cached one. Write the table as a mapping from effect-class to a freshness requirement the src.do consumer enforces.

## The table to produce

| effect class | freshness requirement | rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **act** (reserved) | fresh check required; cached attestation refused regardless of age | ADR 0016 walk 5 — the suspended attorney at sign-time |
| **act** (non-reserved supply, e.g. `consign:wholesale`) | ? | C2: supply-face without a signature; lighter than a reserved act |
| **record** | cached within TTL | C5 |
| **read** (demand/access gate) | cached within TTL; an identifier check may suffice | C5 + the `identifier != good standing` law (OpenEvidence's NPI gate, walk 3) |

Fill in the `?` and the actual TTL values. Justify each against a named binder, not in the abstract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Policy table implemented as data (not scattered conditionals), keyed by effect-class.
- [ ] Reserved-act path **cannot** be satisfied by a cached attestation — enforced structurally, tested.
- [ ] TTL values chosen with recorded rationale per effect class.
- [ ] Table maps onto the src.do `cacheTtl`/`staleTtl`/`freshness` contract rather than re-implementing caching.
- [ ] Source-unavailable + reserved act = deny (fail closed), tested.
- [ ] The open-knob item in ADR 0016 Consequences (b) is answered and cross-referenced.

Blocked by the DECISION issue.

## Size: S

title: Held-credential fact store per principal (ADR 0016 C6) — never a dimension node
description:
## Why

ADR 0016 **C6** places four referents in four different homes. This issue builds exactly one of them, and the placement rule is the whole content of the issue — getting it wrong pollutes a reference dimension permanently.

C6, verbatim:
- the **`Credential` class** mints at **schema.org.ai**
- the **credential *concept* node** ("what USPTO Registration *is*") homes at **`credentials.org.ai`** — per-jurisdiction (~51 state bars, ADR 0007 R7)
- the **held-credential *fact*** ("`human_pat` holds a live reg #12,345, in good standing") is **per-principal identity data at id.org.ai** — **"never a `credentials.org.ai` node (ADR 0007 R7: per-entity facts stay out of reference dimensions)"**
- the **issuer roster** is a **live verification source** (C5 modes 1-3) — *"not a hosted G1 Standard"*

**This issue builds the third bullet only.** A store of held-credential facts, per principal, at id.org.ai.

## The rule, stated as a review gate

**Never a dimension node.** If a held-credential fact ends up addressable as a node in `credentials.org.ai`, ADR 0007 R7 has been violated. The dimension holds *what a credential type is*; id.org.ai holds *who holds which one, and what we last observed about it*.

## What to store

- principal ref (`human_…` / `agent_…` / an Organization for entity-held credentials, C4)
- credential type ref -> the `credentials.org.ai` concept node (a **reference**, not a copy of the concept)
- issuer + jurisdiction + registration identifier
- last observed `{ live, goodStanding, holder, asOf }` from `verify()` — an **observation with a timestamp**, not a standing truth
- the derived `reps` view is *not* stored here either (C4/R4)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-principal store implemented at id.org.ai (fits the existing identity data model — `src/server/services/identity/`, `src/server/do/Identity.ts`).
- [ ] Concept nodes referenced by ref; no concept data copied into the fact store.
- [ ] No write path that could create a `credentials.org.ai` node from a held fact.
- [ ] Every cached status carries `asOf`; nothing stored as a bare boolean.
- [ ] Entity-held (dealership) and individual-held (Pat) cases both storable.
- [ ] Tenant scoping consistent with the existing sharded `IdentityDO` (closed bead `id-ixk`).

Blocked by the DECISION issue and the type issue.

## Size: M

title: Implement verify(credential, principal) -> { live, goodStanding, holder, reps } (registry-lookup mode)
description:
## Why

The one interface ADR 0016 C5 names, verbatim: *"One interface, `verify(credential, principal) -> { live, goodStanding, holder, reps }`, sourced by whichever mode `Credential.issuer` records."*

This issue implements it for **mode 1 (registry lookup)** only, consuming the src.do resource contract from the sibling issue. Modes 2-4 are additional src.do sources behind the same interface — that is the point of building one consumer, not N integrations.

## Semantics that must not be flattened

- **`live` and `goodStanding` are two fields, not one.** ADR 0016 C5's `identifier != good standing` law: an NPI/enumeration hit (OpenEvidence's actual gate — NPI-existence against NPPES, no license upload, no board-status check) is acceptable for a *light demand/access* gate but **not** for a reserved act. Collapsing them into one boolean destroys that distinction and would let a suspended attorney sign a filing.
- **`reps` is derived** (C4) — a view over deputized `Representation` edges from the holder, not a stored list. The transaction check is two-part: *holder in good standing* **AND** *actor is an authorized rep of the holder*.
- **Never mints.** Serve-never-home (ADR 0013 R5): the issuer mints and revokes; id.org.ai verifies and serves. `verify()` must have no write path into credential status.
- Face-dependence (C4): access tends entity-held (the dealership's Manheim membership), perform tends individual-held (Pat's bar registration). Both must work; holder = actor is the common perform case.

## The binder to test against

ADR 0016 walk 5, verbatim: *"A suspended attorney at sign-time. Onboarded live at T0; suspended at T1; presents a cached attestation to sign a filing."* Verdict: **CLICKS-WITH-TIEBREAK** — a reserved act demands a fresh good-standing check, never a stale attestation. That scenario is the acceptance test for this issue plus the freshness-policy sibling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `verify(credential, principal) -> { live, goodStanding, holder, reps }` implemented, registry-lookup mode.
- [ ] Sourced through the src.do resource contract — no direct roster fetching in this repo.
- [ ] `live` and `goodStanding` independently settable and independently tested.
- [ ] `reps` derived from deputized Representation edges; no second store.
- [ ] No code path writes credential status.
- [ ] Source-unavailable fails closed with a distinguishable reason (not "not in good standing", not "in good standing").
- [ ] Walk-5 test: T0 verify passes, T1 suspension causes a reserved-act check to deny even with a cached T0 attestation present.

Blocked by the DECISION issue and the src.do contract issue.

## Size: M

title: Define the src.do credential-source resource contract (USPTO OED lookup) — ingest is src.do's scope
description:
## Why

**The roster ingest is NOT id.org.ai's work.** It belongs to the **src.do port** — the already-scoped migration of the legacy drivly `src.do` into a platform-wide, domain-agnostic source-proxy API layer (part of the auto.dev rewrite). This issue defines the **contract** id.org.ai needs from src.do; it does not build an ingest.

Why it cannot be a simple API call anyway (ADR 0016 C5, mode 1, verbatim): the **USPTO OED practitioner roster** is a *"bulk ZIP/CSV of ~53k active practitioners; **no confirmed REST API**"*. So the source needs fetch + unzip + parse + refresh + cache — precisely the shape src.do's declarative source rows model (`basePath`, `fetcher: fetch|scraper|browser`, auth, `cacheTtl`/`staleTtl`, `resources[]`, plus Resource routing with `fallbackStrategy` and a `schema`/`coverage`/`freshness`/`provenance` data contract).

**Do not create the ingest issue in this repo.**

## The contract to define

A src.do **resource** id.org.ai can call:

- **Lookup key:** USPTO registration number (e.g. Pat's reg #12,345 from ADR 0016 walk 1).
- **Response:** `{ status: Active | Suspended | Excluded | Inactive, holder, asOf }`
  - `status` must be the roster's real status vocabulary — not a bool, and not collapsed to "found/not-found". ADR 0016 C5's **`identifier != good standing` law** is exactly this distinction: an enumeration hit (NPPES-style) is not a good-standing check, and a reserved act requires the latter.
  - `holder` — the practitioner identity as the roster states it.
  - `asOf` — when the underlying roster snapshot was taken. Required; without it liveness cannot be evaluated.
- **Freshness guarantee:** a declared TTL / staleness bound on the resource, surfaced to the caller. This is what the effect-class policy table (sibling issue) reads. Maps onto src.do's `cacheTtl` / `staleTtl` + the `freshness` field of the data contract.
- **Miss semantics:** distinguish "not in roster" from "source unavailable". A source outage must not read as an excluded practitioner, and must not read as an active one either — the gate fails closed with a distinguishable reason.

## Generalize it

Write the contract so the same shape serves the other C5 modes as separate src.do resources — NPPES/NPI, state-bar search, vendor PSV (Verifiable/CertifyOS/FSMB), sanctioned partner (AuctionAccess/FinCEN). **id.org.ai builds one consumer interface, not N integrations.**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contract written down in this repo (`docs/` or a types file) as the interface id.org.ai consumes.
- [ ] Status vocabulary, `holder`, `asOf`, freshness bound, and miss/outage semantics all specified.
- [ ] Shape validated against a second mode on paper (NPPES enumeration + a vendor PSV good-standing call) to confirm it generalizes.
- [ ] The cross-repo dependency on the src.do port is named in the epic; **no ingest code in id.org.ai**.
- [ ] Explicit note that federation (OpenID4VCI/VP) is a *future* source type — no live U.S. issuer offers it today (ADR 0016 C5 mode 4).

Blocked by the DECISION issue.

## Size: S

title: Define the credential type: issuer, holder, perform/access scopes, {credentialRef, jurisdiction} gate
description:
## Why

The type is the whole model. ADR 0016 C1/C2/C4 fix its shape; the most important thing the type does is make a wrong design **unrepresentable**.

## Required shape

- **Monadic** (C1): `{ issuer, holder }` — **no represented principal field.** A `Representation` is relational (`{principal, representative, basis, scope}`); a `Credential` is not. If the type has a `principal` field, C1 has been lost. `holder` is a `Human` **or** an `Organization` (C4).
- **Two-faced** (C2): two scope sets — `perform:` (supply — `sign:patent-application`, `file:uspto`, `notarize`, `consign:wholesale`) and `access:` (demand — `manheim:wholesale`, `cm-ecf`, `sealed-dockets`, `openevidence`). Both are `Scope`s from `src/sdk/auth/scope.ts`, carrying the new `source: Mandate | Credential` discriminator (C2 extends ADR 0012 M4).
- **`authorizedReps` is NOT a field** (C4 / ADR 0007 R4): it is a **derived view** over deputized `Representation` edges whose principal is the holder. Storing it duplicates the fact. If it appears as a stored array on the type, C4 has been lost.
- **Jurisdiction-inflected** (C6 / ADR 0007 R7): "state bar" is ~51 distinct concept nodes, not one. California Bar != Texas Bar.

## The gate is never a bool

The check result must be a `{ credentialRef, jurisdiction }` gate — an addressable reference plus the jurisdiction it was verified in — **never a `boolean`**. A bool discards which credential authorized the act, in which jurisdiction, and as of when; ADR 0016 C5's liveness-by-effect-class and the M6 citing field both need that provenance. `authority: 'PatentAttorney'` on the resulting event is a *citation of a specific credential*, not a flag that "some credential passed".

## Also model

- `requiresSigner: <credential-type>` — a **requirement declaration on the act-type** (C3), distinct from the M6 `authority:` citing field on the resulting event. The act declares the requirement; the event cites the fulfilled authority; different fields.
- `requiresAccess: <credential-type>` — the symmetric demand-side declaration.
- Where the credential concept node lives: `credentials.org.ai` (C6, `roles.tsv canon.credentials`, currently `unprovisioned`). id.org.ai holds the *held-fact*, never the concept node.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Type defined using the name chosen in the DECISION issue.
- [ ] No `principal` / represented-party field (C1 enforced by shape).
- [ ] `perform` and `access` scope sets typed as `Scope` with `source: Credential`.
- [ ] `authorizedReps` derived, not stored (C4/R4).
- [ ] Issuer carries jurisdiction (C6/R7).
- [ ] The gate return type is `{ credentialRef, jurisdiction, ... }` — a `boolean` return is a review failure.
- [ ] Type-level tests instantiate all four ADR 0016 binders: USPTO reg (individual, perform-heavy), Manheim dealer (entity, both faces), RON notary (individual, perform), physician NPI (individual, access-only).

Blocked by the DECISION issue.

## Size: M

title: DECISION: settle the ADR 0016 M-d rename — Credential collides with client_credentials
description:
**Type: DECISION. This blocks every other child of this epic.**

## Why

ADR 0016 flags the collision itself (Consequences, **M-d**), verbatim:

> **Naming-collision flag (likely rename at graduation, M-d).** In identity systems "credential" already means the **presented auth artifact** — ADR 0013 (`:75`) resolves *"the identity behind the presented credential,"* and C5 builds on **OpenID4VCI/VP "Verifiable Credentials."** At id.org.ai, `Credential` (professional licensure) would collide with credential (login/VC artifact). Pre-staged rename candidates for the naturalness check: **`Licensure` · `Qualification` · `Warrant` · `Practice-Right`.**

**id.org.ai is precisely where the collision bites**, because this repo already uses the other sense:
- OAuth 2.1 `client_credentials` grant (`worker/routes/oauth.ts`, `src/sdk/oauth/clients.ts`)
- API keys, Ed25519 agent keypairs, JWTs — all "credentials" in the presented-artifact sense
- `AuthBroker.identify()` resolves *the identity behind the presented credential* (`src/sdk/auth/broker-impl.ts:276`)

Writing `verify(credential, principal)` into a codebase where `credential` already means "the bearer token on this request" produces a permanent reading hazard in the most security-sensitive file in the repo.

## The decision to make

Pick the runtime name for the ADR 0016 professional-licensure primitive as it appears in id.org.ai code:

| Candidate | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| `Credential` (keep) | matches the ADR verbatim; no translation layer | collides with the auth-artifact sense already in this repo |
| `Licensure` | precise; matches "issuer-granted standing authorization"; zero collision | slightly formal; is a dealer's Manheim membership a "licensure"? |
| `Qualification` | broad enough for bar + dealer + notary + CPA | vague; overlaps `Capability` (can-do) in reading |
| `Warrant` | short; carries "issued authority" | collides with the legal-instrument sense (a warrant is a court order) |
| `Practice-Right` | most descriptive of the perform-face | hyphenated; awkward as a type name; weak fit for the access-face |

**Test the candidates against ADR 0016's own binders**, not in the abstract: Pat's USPTO reg #12,345 (walk 1), the Manheim dealer license via AuctionAccess (walk 2, the keystone), the RON notary commission (walk 4), the OpenEvidence physician gate (walk 3). A name that reads naturally for the patent bar but not for a dealership membership fails C2's supply/demand symmetry.

## Also decide

- Whether the ADR-level term stays `Credential` in org.ai while the id.org.ai runtime uses the renamed term (a translation seam), or the ADR is amended.
- The disambiguating name for the *other* sense in this repo, if any (`presented credential` -> `auth artifact`?).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One name chosen, with the reasoning recorded against the four named binders.
- [ ] Recorded in `id.org.ai/docs/adr/` (a short ADR or an addendum) and cross-referenced from org.ai ADR 0016 M-d.
- [ ] The org.ai-term-vs-runtime-term question answered explicitly.
- [ ] Sibling issues updated to use the chosen name before implementation starts.

## Size: S

title: Replace the hardcoded LEVEL_CAPABILITIES ladder with structured Scope (supersedes id-lkj)
description:
## Why

Authorization is currently a **hardcoded ladder**: capability level -> a fixed list of strings.

**Current state:**
- `src/sdk/mcp/auth.ts:52` — `const LEVEL_SCOPES: Record<CapabilityLevel, string[]>`
- `src/sdk/mcp/auth.ts:60` — `const LEVEL_CAPABILITIES: Record<CapabilityLevel, string[]>`
- consumed at `src/sdk/mcp/auth.ts:113-114`, `:144-145`, `:200-201`, `:223-224`
- `worker/middleware/require-scope.ts` — the worker-side gate over the same ladder

A fixed table cannot express `ScopeGrant { verb, resource, ceiling }`. It cannot express a resource pattern, a spend ceiling, or a per-credential narrowing — all of which `src/sdk/auth/scope.ts` already models (`resourceMatches:111`, `scopeSatisfies:192`, `narrows:206`, `deriveChildScope:226`).

It also cannot express what Epic 4 needs: a scope whose `source` is a `Credential` rather than a `Mandate` (ADR 0016 C2 extends ADR 0012 M4 with exactly that discriminator).

## Supersedes

**Parked bead `id-lkj`** — *"Replace LEVEL_SCOPES ladder with WorkOS FGA tuple checks"* (closed). That framing pinned the replacement to a specific vendor. This issue supersedes it: the replacement is the repo's own structured `Scope`, with FGA remaining an option for the async `need.resource` path (already routed through `gate()` per `broker-impl.ts:274-280`), not the whole model.

## What to do

- Derive scopes from the structured `Scope` on the agent/key (Epic 3a) instead of indexing a level into a table.
- Keep `CapabilityLevel` as a *tier* concept (it is public via the ladder declared in `/.well-known/agents.json`, Epic 1a) — but let the tier map to a default `Scope`, not to a frozen string list.
- Update `worker/middleware/require-scope.ts` to call `scopeSatisfies` with a `ScopeRequirement`.
- Leave room for `ScopeGrant.source: Mandate | Credential` (ADR 0016 C2) without implementing credentials here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `LEVEL_CAPABILITIES` removed; `LEVEL_SCOPES` reduced to a tier-default `Scope` (or removed).
- [ ] All six consumption sites in `src/sdk/mcp/auth.ts` migrated.
- [ ] `worker/middleware/require-scope.ts` gates via `scopeSatisfies`.
- [ ] Deny-path tests from the sibling issue still pass, plus new ones for resource-pattern and ceiling denial.
- [ ] Externally observable behavior at each of L0-L3 is unchanged (regression tests) — this is a refactor of the mechanism, not of the policy.
- [ ] `npm test` green.

Depends on the `Agent.scope` sibling issue.

## Size: M

title: Structured 402 offers at paid boundaries
description:
## Why

AX check **8**: payment boundaries are structured 402 offers. AXP requires *"hard-ceiling metered pricing"* (`ax/CONTEXT.md`). An agent hitting a paid boundary should receive a machine-readable offer, not an opaque 403.

Also relevant: the **Spend Ceiling** vs **Rate Limit** distinction is already ratified vocabulary (`ax/CONTEXT.md`): a rate limit is refilled by the clock and paying cannot refill it; a spend ceiling is refilled only by settlement and routes to payment. A 402 offer belongs to the spend-ceiling path only. `src/server/services/keys/rate-limit.ts` is the clock path and must NOT emit 402.

## Honest state of the rail

**The Stripe rail is a confirmed stub.** `src/sdk/oauth/stripe.ts` is minimal. This issue does **not** require a working charge; api.qa's check 8 is presence-grade in the MVP (`DESIGN.md` attack #11 names 402 `declared-only` as a named residual, with behavioral paid-boundary probes as a seam).

So scope this as: **structured, honest 402 offers at a real boundary** — and do not claim a settlement capability the stub does not have (`claims-honesty`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least one real boundary answers `402` with a structured offer body (price, unit, ceiling, how to settle).
- [ ] Rate-limit exhaustion answers `429`/retry-later, never 402 — the two enforcers stay distinct.
- [ ] The 402 boundary is declared in the OpenAPI document so api.qa can probe it.
- [ ] The offer does not overstate the Stripe stub's capability.
- [ ] api.qa check 8 passes.

## Size: M

title: Publish OpenAPI 3.1 for the real surface (/auth/verify, /agent/*, /api/keys, /oauth/*, /mcp)
description:
## Why

AX check **5**: machine-readable contract published. api.qa's fixed surface plan looks for a declared OpenAPI document or falls back to `/openapi.json`, then **seeded endpoint sampling** probes it (api.qa `DESIGN.md`, attack #4: the seed is fresh per run and unpredictable — you cannot overfit to a known probe set).

## Scope — the real surface only

Document what the worker actually routes (`worker/routes/`):
- `/auth/verify` (`worker/routes/auth-verify.ts`)
- `/agent/*` (`worker/routes/aap.ts` — the AAP wire surface)
- `/api/keys` (`worker/routes/api-keys.ts`)
- `/oauth/*` (`worker/routes/oauth.ts` — OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + device flow)
- `/mcp` (`worker/routes/mcp.ts`)

OpenAPI **3.1**, not 3.0.

## The warning, restated because it lands here

This document is what arms `schema-conformance` and `claims-honesty`. Both are non-scoring and both **cap the grade at C** when they fail (api.qa `DESIGN.md` attack #11). Concretely:
- every path documented must exist and route (claims-honesty)
- every documented response schema must match what a sampled call actually returns (schema-conformance)
- error shapes count: the standardized error format (closed bead `id-l71`) must be what the schemas say

Prefer omitting an endpoint you cannot describe accurately over documenting it optimistically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] OpenAPI 3.1 document served (and linked from `/llms.txt` and `/.well-known/agents.json`).
- [ ] All five surface groups above documented, request + response schemas included.
- [ ] api.qa check 5 passes.

- [ ] Grade did not regress from the Epic 1 result.

title: Verify with api.qa — target AX score >= 7/10, zero honesty failures
description:

title: GS1 Digital Link resolver (org.ai ADR 0013 / id ADR 0001)
description:
## Why

org.ai **ADR 0013** rules that id.org.ai *is* the GS1 Digital Link resolver, that the resolver is the GET face of the authority membrane, and that — because it is the identity layer — it supplies the authenticated **Who** that completes EPCIS's 5W+H natively (R3, the load-bearing thesis). `id.gs1.org` resolves anonymously by policy; id.org.ai resolves identity-complete.

id.org.ai **ADR 0001** is the companion build ADR. It states the current position bluntly: *"This repo currently has **no resolver code** (greenfield)."*

And it states the one non-obvious build fact, verbatim:

> **we already have the Who.** `AuthBroker.identify(req)` (`broker-impl.ts:276`) resolves the principal from any request's credential, returning the L0 anonymous identity when none is presented and never throwing. The resolver does not need a new identity mechanism — it needs to route GS1 keys through the broker and attach the resolved principal to the staged/captured event.

## Governing principle: superset, not limitation

ADR 0013 R1 — conform **completely** at the seam (a stock GS1 scanner and a stock EPCIS repository must interoperate with zero knowledge of us), and let the native model be a **strict superset**: the authenticated `Who`, agent principals as first-class scanners, the membrane, the native 5W+H `Event`. *"The seam is lossy downward, never upward."* Conformance is a floor; it never caps us.

## Two more laws that constrain every child

- **The Digital Link URI is an address, never an `$id`** (R2, reconciled with R5). `https://id.org.ai/01/{gtin}/21/{serial}` resolves *to* the object's canonical `{type}_{sqid}` `$id`; the emitted JSON-LD carries that `$id` with the GS1 URI as its `sameAs`.
- **Serve, never home** (R5): GS1 homes GTIN allocation — the platform never mints GTINs. `id.gs1.org` stays GS1-canonical and fallback.

## Conformance targets

GS1-Conformant Resolver Standard; GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax; **RFC 9264** Linkset. Verified 2026-07-20.

## Blocked by

**Epic 3 (ADR 0012 M5 authz-path realignment).** id.org.ai ADR 0001 **D6** aligns the resolver's authorization vocabulary to ADR 0012: the resolved principal is `human_…`/`agent_…` and its authorization is a **`Scope` at a tier, not a `Capability`**. Building the membrane's tier gating on `capabilities: string[]` means rebuilding it.

## Size: L (epic)

title: Credential verification runtime (ADR 0016 C5) — the AuctionAccess role
description:
## Why

**ADR 0016 C5 assigns credential verification to id.org.ai.** Verbatim from the ADR's blast radius: *"id.org.ai — the verifier / aggregator (the AuctionAccess role). **[forced-to-build]** implement `verify()` with the C5 modes, the *ordered* M8->`requiresSigner` supply gate and the `requiresAccess` demand gate (C3), liveness-by-effect-class, and the held-credential identity-fact store (C6)."*

The model, compressed:
- A **`Credential`** is **monadic** — `{issuer, holder}`, *no represented principal* (C1). That is what distinguishes it from a `Representation` (relational: `{principal, representative, basis, scope}`) and from a `Mandate`-granted `Scope`. Pat's USPTO bar registration represents no one until Dana separately grants a POA.
- It is **two-faced** (C2): `perform:` scopes (supply side — `sign:patent-application`, `consign:wholesale`) and `access:` scopes (demand side — `manheim:wholesale`, `cm-ecf`, `openevidence`). Both are `Scope`s carrying a new `source: Mandate | Credential` discriminator.
- It has **two levels** (C4): a `holder` (Human or Organization) plus a **derived** `authorizedReps` view over deputized `Representation` edges — never a stored field (ADR 0007 R4: derived edges own nothing).
- Verification is **liveness-by-effect-class** (C5): a reserved act needs a **fresh** good-standing check; read/record may use a cached attestation with a TTL.
- **Serve, never home** (ADR 0013 R5): the issuer mints and revokes; **the platform never mints a credential.**

## Scope correction: id.org.ai verifies and enforces — it does NOT ingest

All four ADR 0016 C5 verification modes become **src.do source types**, not id.org.ai integrations:

| C5 mode | src.do source type | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Registry lookup | `fetch` / `scraper` source | USPTO OED roster, NPPES/NPI, state-bar public search |
| 2. Vendor-brokered PSV | `fetch` source with auth | Verifiable, CertifyOS, Medallion, FSMB PDC/FCVS, CAQH |
| 3. Sanctioned partner | `fetch` source with partner token | FinCEN S2S, IRS A2A, USPTO Patent Center, AuctionAccess |
| 4. Federated OAuth/OIDC | future source type | OpenID4VCI/VP — **not live at any U.S. issuer today** (C5) |

The **src.do port** (migrating the legacy drivly `src.do` into a platform-wide, domain-agnostic source-proxy API layer, part of the auto.dev rewrite) models exactly this: declarative source rows with `basePath`, a `fetcher` type (`fetch` | `scraper` | `browser`), auth headers/token, `cacheTtl` / `staleTtl`, and `resources[]`; plus a Resource routing layer with `fallbackStrategy` and the `schema` / `coverage` / `freshness` / `provenance` data contract.

Two consequences that materially shrink this epic:
1. **id.org.ai builds ONE consumer interface, not N integrations.** `verify(credential, principal)` sits over src.do resources.
2. **ADR 0016's liveness-by-effect-class maps directly onto src.do's `cacheTtl` / `staleTtl` + the `freshness` field of the data contract.** A reserved act demands a fresh read; read/record can accept a cached one. The policy table (child issue) is a mapping onto an existing mechanism, not a new caching layer.

## External dependency (cross-repo, not tracked here)

**The src.do port.** Roster/registry ingest, scraping, fetcher plumbing, and cache/staleness enforcement are **src.do's scope**. Do not create ingest issues in this repo. This epic defines the *contract* id.org.ai needs from src.do and consumes it.

## Blocked by

- **Epic 3 (ADR 0012 M5 authz-path realignment)** — ADR 0016 states the credential gates are *"the same authz path"*. `requiresSigner` / `requiresAccess` are `Scope` checks with `source: Credential`; they cannot be built on `capabilities: string[]`.
- **The naming DECISION child issue** — the type cannot be written under a name that is about to change.

## Naming hazard (ADR 0016 M-d)

In identity systems "credential" already means the presented auth artifact. ADR 0013 (`:75`) says *"the identity behind the presented credential"*, and this repo's OAuth surface uses `client_credentials`. See the DECISION child.

title: AXP Tier 1: contract + commerce
description:
## Why

Tier 0 (Epic 1) publishes *that* id.org.ai has surfaces. Tier 1 publishes *what the contract is* and *what things cost* — AX checks **5** (machine-readable contract published), **8** (payment boundaries are structured 402 offers), and the linkset half of **9**.

This is where the AXP (`ax/CONTEXT.md`, "Agent eXperience Protocol"): *"OpenAPI 3.1 + llms.txt + markdown-first typed bodies + typed BLOCKED/EMPTY errors + hard-ceiling metered pricing + a resolver-addressable home, served with content negotiation and keyless first value"* actually binds. apis.ax publishes AXP; api.qa enforces it.

## The standing hazard for this epic

Publishing a contract **arms** api.qa's two grade-capping honesty checks:
- `schema-conformance` — sampled responses must match the published schemas
- `claims-honesty` — claimed endpoints must exist

Either failing **caps the grade at C regardless of score** (api.qa `DESIGN.md` attack #11: *"a lying surface is worse than a missing one"*). Epic 1 can reach B with no OpenAPI at all. A careless OpenAPI here can therefore **lower** the grade. Publish the real surface, narrowly and accurately.

Note also attack #3: shrinking the claims to dodge the honesty checks lowers the score too (grading rewards verified richness). The only winning move is an accurate contract.

`id.org.ai/specs/axp-acceptance.spec.json` (api.qa PinnedSpec, authored in parallel) plus a deployed-verifier run. Do not block on the spec file existing.

title: Fix the flaky test/auth-verify-token.test.ts — last-char base64url tamper is a no-op
description:
## Why

`test/auth-verify-token.test.ts` fails intermittently. **It is a test bug, not a security hole** — but it keeps `npm test` at 1805/1806 and poisons the "green suite" gate that Epics 3, 4 and 5 all rely on.

## Root cause (diagnosed)

The tamper flips the **last** base64url character of an Ed25519 signature:

- `test/auth-verify-token.test.ts:96` — `const flipped = sig.slice(0, -1) + (sig.at(-1) === 'A' ? 'B' : 'A')`
- `test/auth-verify-token.test.ts:213` — the same expression inline: `` const tampered = `${parts[0]}.${parts[1]}.${sig.slice(0, -1) + (sig.at(-1) === 'A' ? 'B' : 'A')}` ``

An Ed25519 signature is **64 bytes = 512 bits**. Base64url encodes 6 bits per character, so 64 bytes needs 86 characters carrying 516 bits — the final character contributes only **4 significant bits**, and its **low 4 bits are padding**. Flipping the last character between `A` and `B` changes only those padding bits: the decoded 64-byte signature is **byte-identical**, so the signature still verifies correctly and the "rejects a tampered signature" assertion fails.

It is intermittent because it depends on the signature the key happens to produce for that run — some encodings differ in the significant bits of the last character, some do not.

## The fix

**Tamper a mid-signature character** instead of the last one — any index safely inside the string, where all 6 bits are significant. Flip it to a different base64url character (guarding against flipping to itself).

Apply at both sites (`:96` and `:213`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both tamper sites mutate a mid-signature character, not the last.
- [ ] The flip is guaranteed to produce a different character (no accidental no-op).
- [ ] The tampered signature provably decodes to different bytes — assert that, so the test cannot silently regress to a no-op tamper again.
- [ ] Test run 50x consecutively with no failure (it is currently intermittent; one green run proves nothing).
- [ ] `npm test` green at **1806/1806**.
- [ ] Note in the commit that this was a test bug, not a verification weakness — `verifyToken` was correct throughout.

title: EPCIS 2.0 capture/query seam
description:
## Why

ADR 0013 R1 requires that *"a stock EPCIS repository sees … valid documents"* and ADR 0001 **D5** commits the repo to the EPCIS 2.0 capture/query surface. Without it, the Who-completion has nowhere to land and the two named consumers — **epcis.dev** (the B2A/B2D developer/agent conformance + event-registry face) and **visibility.cloud** (the B2B supply-chain-executive face) — have nothing to consume.

## Conformance floor + superset delta

- Emit and accept **valid EPCIS 2.0** documents; **CBV bizSteps verbatim** for real supply-chain steps (R6 — a `dispensing` or `receiving` scan is exactly that).
- **CBV extension verbs on the R17 extension lane** for the cases that are *not* supply-chain steps: a consumer authenticity check and an agent dereference-for-provenance take `inspecting` / `verifying`. R6, verbatim: *"so they are real EPCIS events that never masquerade as `receiving`. Superset in miniature: our verb set ⊇ CBV."*
- **The seam is lossy downward, never upward** (R1): emitting to a stock EPCIS repository degrades the first-class `Who` into EPCIS's weak party fields; the complete `Who` is retained natively. Do not let the seam's weakness propagate inward — the native `Event` keeps the full principal ref.

## Also

- Events land in the object's **owning startup's G5 books** (R17, R4).
- The SGTIN maps to `epc` / `urn:epc:id:sgtin:…` as a **sanctioned alias** (ADR 0013, schema.org.ai row) — never a rebase of our grammar on foreign keys (R17).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] EPCIS 2.0 **capture** endpoint accepts valid EPCIS documents.
- [ ] EPCIS 2.0 **query** endpoint answers conformantly.
- [ ] A stock EPCIS repository can consume our emitted documents (validated against the standard, not just against ourselves).
- [ ] CBV bizSteps used verbatim for supply-chain steps.
- [ ] `inspecting` / `verifying` extension verbs used for consumer-check and agent-dereference events; neither masquerades as `receiving`.
- [ ] Downward degradation of `Who` -> party fields is explicit and tested; the native event retains the first-class principal.
- [ ] SGTIN <-> `urn:epc:id:sgtin:` alias mapping round-trips.

title: Cache SigningKeyManager at module level
description: In worker/index.ts, own JWT verification creates a new SigningKeyManager per request and calls oauthStub.oauthStorageOp() to load keys from the DO. The manager has an in-memory cache (loaded flag) but a new instance is created each time across requests. Every JWT verification hits IdentityDO storage at least once per request. Fix: cache the SigningKeyManager or its JWKS data at module level, similar to auth-verifier's jwksCache pattern.

close_reason: PARKED — long lead time, upstream-PR-driven.
